units.title: Reading fiction texts
units.description: Analyse character, setting, narrative viewpoint and writer's methods in fiction extracts.
units.generationNotes: Use a short original fictional extract in each practice item. Do not imitate or reproduce copyrighted exam texts. Ask about evidence, inference and effect.

objectives.text: Read and understand extracts, making inferences and selecting relevant evidence.

units.title: Reading non-fiction texts
units.description: Understand viewpoints, arguments, information and persuasive choices in non-fiction writing.
units.generationNotes: Use short original non-fiction stimuli. Keep claims fictional or clearly framed as text evidence. Distinguish what the writer says from what the reader infers.

objectives.text: Read and understand non-fiction texts, identifying viewpoints, purposes and supporting evidence.

units.title: Language analysis
units.description: Identify and explain how writers use vocabulary, imagery, figurative language and sentence choices for effect.
units.generationNotes: Use original two-sentence stimuli. Require a word or phrase, a precise effect and a link to context; avoid unsupported claims about author intention.

objectives.text: Analyse how language choices shape meaning and response.

units.title: Structure and form
units.description: Explain how beginnings, shifts, endings, paragraphing and text form organise a reader's experience.
units.generationNotes: Use original short stimuli with clearly stated positions or sequence. Ask about structural effect, not hidden author biography.

objectives.text: Analyse how structure and form organise texts and develop meaning.

units.title: Creative writing
units.description: Plan and craft descriptive or narrative writing with purposeful vocabulary, structure, sentence control and accurate punctuation.
units.generationNotes: Teach planning and editing rather than claiming a mark. Practice prompts must ask for a small writing decision or revision, not a full essay. Include self-review language.

objectives.text: Communicate imaginative ideas using effective vocabulary, structure, sentence control and accurate spelling and punctuation.

units.title: Transactional writing
units.description: Write for a stated audience and purpose using appropriate register, organisation, evidence and persuasive or informative choices.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional audiences and situations. Practice should distinguish purpose, audience, register and evidence. Do not claim that a response meets an official mark scheme.

objectives.text: Write clearly and coherently for different purposes and audiences using appropriate tone, organisation and evidence.

units.title: Spelling, punctuation and grammar
units.description: Apply sentence boundaries, punctuation, spelling and grammatical choices to communicate clearly and accurately.
units.generationNotes: Use original sentences and short editing tasks. Explain the grammatical reason for each correction. Include varied sentence structures without treating one style as universally correct.

objectives.text: Use standard English grammar, punctuation and spelling accurately and deliberately.
